text:
Actor Kim Soo-hyun appeared in court Wednesday as a witness in the trial of Kim Se-ui, head of the YouTube channel Garo Sero Research Institute, who was indicted while in custody on charges of spreading false information about the actor's private life.
The Seoul Central District Court's Criminal Division 26, presided over by Judge Lee Hyun-kyung, held the first hearing in Kim Se-ui's trial on Wednesday. He faces charges including defamation under the Information and Communications Network Act and violations of laws against sexual violence and stalking.
Kim Soo-hyun arrived at the courthouse at around 1:40 p.m. to testify. However, he entered the courtroom through a separate passage rather than the main entrance, where reporters were waiting.
His testimony was conducted behind closed doors because the case involves alleged violations of the Sexual Violence Punishment Act.
The trial stems from controversy surrounding Kim Soo-hyun's private life that erupted last year.
At the time, Garo Sero Research Institute, operated by Kim Se-ui, alleged that Kim Soo-hyun had dated the late actor Kim Sae-ron when she was a minor. The allegations spread widely online, placing Kim Soo-hyun at the center of controversy and prompting him to suspend his entertainment activities.
However, the case took a turn after police cleared Kim Soo-hyun of allegations of violating the Child Welfare Act and making false accusations, deciding not to refer the case to prosecutors.
Meanwhile, Kim Se-ui, who had raised the allegations, was indicted while in custody on charges including defamation.
Prosecutors also accused Kim Se-ui of distributing an AI-manipulated recording purporting to feature Kim Sae-ron's voice and threatening Kim Soo-hyun.
Kim Se-ui was indicted in June and currently denies all charges.
